name: Pediatric direct ulnar approach to the distal ulna
corridor: Longitudinal ECU-FCU interval with explicit dorsal sensory ulnar-nerve protection

positioning.text: Position supine with arm on a radiolucent hand table and forearm positioned for direct ulnar access.

setup.text: Localize the distal-ulnar physis and DRUJ, assess remaining growth and associated radius injury, and map the dorsal sensory nerve.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark ulna, ulnar styloid, physis under imaging, ECU, FCU, and DRUJ.

incision.text: Make a longitudinal incision over the distal ulna between ECU and FCU, centered on the fracture and kept no longer than needed.

superficial_interval.text: Seek and protect the dorsal sensory ulnar-nerve branch before developing the ECU-FCU interval.

deep_interval.text: Release only necessary ulnar extensor retinaculum and expose the fracture with minimal periosteal and physeal stripping.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous sensory-nerve plane, ECU-FCU interval, retinaculum, periosteum, then distal ulna and physis.

structures_encountered.text: Dorsal sensory ulnar nerve, ECU, FCU, extensor retinaculum, ulnar styloid, distal-ulnar physis, and DRUJ are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Dorsal sensory nerve, ulnar physis and blood supply, ECU sheath, TFCC, DRUJ cartilage, and ulnar neurovascular bundle are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Avoid repeated physeal manipulation, transphyseal thermal injury, and circumferential epiphyseal stripping; distal-ulnar growth arrest can produce major variance and deformity.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid traction on the dorsal sensory branch and forceful ECU or TFCC retraction.

exposure.text: Provides direct access to pediatric distal-ulna, styloid, and physeal fractures while permitting DRUJ assessment.

limitations.text: Does not expose the radius and cannot substitute for longitudinal surveillance after a physeal injury.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along ulna or add a separate radius/DRUJ exposure while preserving nerve and physeal tissues.

indications.text: Use selectively for irreducible or unstable displaced distal-ulnar physeal, neck, or styloid injuries requiring open control.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid open exposure when acceptable stable closed reduction is achievable and avoid unnecessary fixation of stable small fragments.

implant_implications.text: Choose low-profile, physeal-respecting fixation, avoid joint penetration, and plan removal when growth or implant position warrants it.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm physeal alignment, ulnar variance, DRUJ congruity, and implant containment on orthogonal views.

closure.text: Repair retinaculum, confirm ECU glide and DRUJ stability, and close without injuring or trapping the dorsal sensory branch.

complications.text: Complications include growth arrest, ulnar variance and deformity, DRUJ instability, sensory neuroma, tendon irritation, infection, and nonunion.

bailouts.text: Use a separate approach for associated radius pathology and institute long-term growth surveillance even after satisfactory fixation.

procedure_applications.condition: A displaced distal-ulna or physeal fracture requires open reduction or stable fixation

questions.question: Which nerve branch must be protected?
questions.answer: The dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve.

questions.question: What long-term complication requires surveillance?
questions.answer: Distal-ulnar growth arrest with altered ulnar variance.
